The task is to analyze the structure of a Bachata set $S$ and determine if it is uniquely determined by the closure properties.

A Bachata set $S$ must satisfy:
1. $0 \in S$.
2. If $n \in S$, then $n + 11 \in S$ and $n + 20 \in S$.

This structure implies that $S$ is an additive sub-semigroup of $(\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}, +)$, generated by $\{11, 20\}$ and containing 0.

If $S$ is a Bachata set, then $S$ must contain all numbers formed by starting at 0 and repeatedly adding 11 or 20. Let $G$ be the set of all non-negative integer linear combinations of 11 and 20:
$$G = \{ 11k + 20l \mid k, l \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0} \}.$$
By definition, $G \subseteq S$.

Conversely, if $m \in S$, then $m$ must have been constructed from 0 by a finite sequence of additions of 11 and 20. Therefore, $m$ must be in $G$. Thus, $S \subseteq G$.

Since $G \subseteq S$ and $S \subseteq G$, we conclude that $S$ must be uniquely determined as $S = G$.

I will record this structural finding in the notes.
